457411.title: Sleep Disorders
457411.description: Sleep research and sleep medicine have grown rapidly over the last thirty years, partly as a result of the discovery that REM (rapid eye movement) sleep coincided with dreaming and partly because of the discovery of sleep apnea (breathing stopping during sleep). Countries vary in how they deal with sleep disorders; in the U.S. sleep medicine is recognised as a field and it is looked after by the National Heart, Lung and Blood Institute; other medical specialities e.g. neurology, pulmonology, psychiatry, may be influential in other countries.   The sleep disorders category is broadly divided into sub-categories that deal with the specific sleep disorders as well as the institutions that regulate, diagnose and treat these disorders. Sleep is affected by the brain's biological clock and so is included in this category. Shift-work sleep disorder and jet-lag are well-known problems that reflect the activity of the biological clock.   This category consists of some of the major 'omnibus' sites (SleepNet, Brain Information Service, Sleep Medicine and the SleepWell) that can contain just about everything (information, chats, consultations, portals, etc). It also lists smaller, general information sites as well as sites that provide short and concise general sleep disorders information.    The Organisations sub-category is packed with information that is more specific to particular sleep disorders. Apart from listing the various centers, the Sleep Centers sub-category is worth visiting as many of these sites provide useful information on sleep disorders.   Anyone with health concerns is reminded that it is advisable to discuss their problems with a licensed medical professional.

455319.description: Individual sites for dentist offices and practices are listed under the appropriate category in the Regional/ section of the Directory.       Restorative dentistry, also known as operative dentistry, is concerned with the restoration of defects or carries in individual teeth.       Cosmetic dentistry is purely aesthetic and involves bleaching, bonding, veneers, reshaping, orthodontics, or implants.       Prosthetic dentistry includes implants.       Pediatric dentistry includes all services defined in the 'general practice' category, for children.       Orthodontics deals with problems in the alignment of teeth and jaws.       Endodontics is concerned with the morphology, physiology and pathology of the human dental pulp and periradicular tissues and root canal treatments.       Periodontics is concerned with the prevention, diagnosis and treatment of diseases affecting the gums and supporting structures of the teeth.       Oral surgery refers to extractions.

455338.title: Temporomandibular Joint Syndrome
455338.description:
"TMJ" stands for temporomandibular joint, or the jaw joint. The TMJs are the small joints in front of each ear that attach the lower jaw (mandible) to the skull. They allow you to perform such functions as opening and closing your mouth, chewing, speaking, and swallowing.

TMJ diseases and disorders refer to a set of conditions, manifested by pain in the area of the jaw and associated muscles and limitations in the ability to make the normal movements of speech, facial expression, eating, chewing, and swallowing. Conditions that routinely affect other joints in the body, such as arthritis and trauma, also affect the TM joint.

455327.title: Oral Surgery
455327.description: Since 1990, the ADA has defined oral and maxillofacial surgery  as "the specialty of dentistry which includes the diagnosis, surgical and adjunctive treatment of diseases, injuries and defects involving both the functional and esthetic aspects of the hard and soft tissues of the oral and maxillofacial region.    Oral and Maxillofacial Surgeons in the US and many other nations have 4 to 7 years of hospital based residency training following the 4 year dental curriculum and receipt of the DDS or DMD degree. They treat conditions, defects, injuries, and esthetic aspects of the mouth, teeth, jaws, and face. It involves caring for patients who have problem wisdom teeth, facial pain, and misaligned jaws. Oral and maxillofacial surgeons also treat accident victims suffering facial injuries, offer reconstructive and dental implant surgery, and care for patients with tumors and cysts of the head and neck. 452674.title: Evidence Based Medicine
452674.description: Evidence-based Medicine (EBM) is an approach that encourages the employment of the best available clinical evidence from systematic research for use in clinical practice. It seeks to augment medical traditions not yet subjected to adequate evaluation with findings based on the application of the scientific method. EBM tools include, but are not limited to, randomized controlled trials, systematic reviews (of a series of trials) and meta-analyses.

links.title: Finding Grey Literature Evidence and Assessing for Outcome and Analysis Reporting Biases When Comparing Medical Interventions
links.description: Guidelines for when and how to search, and assess, "grey literature" (typically non-peer-reviewed conference abstracts, books, dissertations, regulatory reports, etc.) when conducting a systematic review or meta-analysis. From Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality (AHRQ). [2013]

links.title: How to Do Random Allocation (Randomization)
links.description: Describes and illustrates with practical examples the concept and procedure of random allocation as used in randomized controlled trials/studies (RCTs), including simple, block and stratified randomization. [2014]

links.title: Worth Adapting? Revisiting the Usefulness of Outcome-Adaptive Randomization
links.description: Describes the potential superiority in well-defined cases of adaptive randomization which allocates more patients to the better treatments as the data accumulates in the trial. [2012]

links.title: I-SPY 2 may change how clinical trials are conducted
links.description: Describes I-SPY, a groundbreaking dynamic adaptive randomization model for accelerating both identification and regulatory approval of effective investigational agents. [2013]

links.title: Evidence-based mapping of design heterogeneity prior to meta-analys
links.description: Demonstrates an assessment of sugar-sweetened beverages and type 2 diabetes as an example to show how the new technique called ‘evidence mapping’ can be used to organize studies and evaluate design heterogeneity prior to meta-analysis. [2014]

links.title: Evidence-Based Medicine
links.description: Concise review of the essential concepts and implementation of evidence-based medicine. [2014]

links.title: A randomised controlled trial of a blended learning education intervention for teaching evidence-based medicine
links.description: Clinical trial comparing a blended learning (BL) versus didactic learning (DL) approach for teaching EBM, concluding that a multifaceted approach incorporating BL may be best suited for medical students. [2015]

links.title: Systematic reviews and meta-analyses: a step-by-step guide
links.description: Detailed guidance on how to conduct a systematic review or meta-analysis, with accompanying lectures developed by the University of Edinburgh's Centre for Cognitive Ageing and Cognitive Epidemiology (CCACE).

links.title: Systematic reviews and meta-analysis of preclinical studies
links.description: Discusses and details the important concept of conducting systematic reviews and meta-analyses for preclinical (in vitro and in vovo) research. [2014]

links.title: The Usefulness of Systematic Reviews of Animal Experiments for the Design of Preclinical and Clinical Studies
links.description: Details how the design, conduct, and analysis of animal experiments may be optimized through the use of systematic reviews. [2014]

links.title: Introduction to Meta Analysis
links.description: Comprehensive guide to conducting a meta-analysis, including a detailed case study (43 pp.). [2014]

links.title: Adaptive design methods in clinical trials - a review
links.description: A review of adaptive clinical trial design and adpative randomization, examining their impact, challenges, obstacles, and strategies for effective deployment. [2008]

links.title: Adaptive Clinical Trials: The Promise and the Caution
links.description: Critically examines the potential benefits and disadvantages of adaptive trial designs, which use accumulating results in the trial to modify the trial's course. [2010]

links.title: Ethical concerns about adaptive randomization
links.description: Raises serious questions about the ethical propriety of adaptive designs where the probability of being assigned to one treatment versus its comparator is dependent on emerging data. [2015]

links.title: Appraisal Tools for Clinical Practice Guidelines: A Systematic Review
links.description: Systematic review of guideline appraisal tools identifying and comparing existing tools and their relative degrees of validation. [2013]

links.title: Guidelines 2.0: systematic development of a comprehensive checklist for a successful guideline enterprise
links.description: Compilation of a comprehensive checklist of items linked to the relevant resources and tools that guideline developers should consider. [2014]

links.title: Observational Evidence and Strength of Evidence Domains: Case Examples
links.description: Demonstrates how observational studies may provide moderate- to (rarely) high-strength evidence in systematic reviews. [2014]

links.title: Random Allocation in Controlled Clinical Trials: A Review
links.description: An update on and clarification of various random allocation techniques, especially simple randomization, blocking, stratified random allocation, and minimization, and a critique of non-random approaches. [2014]

links.title: Observational and interventional study design types; an overview | Biochemia Medica
links.description: Review of the strengths and weaknesses of observational versus interventional study design. [2014]

links.title: Meta-analysis in medical research
links.description: An introduction to and rationale for meta-analysis, including presentation, interpretation, and biases. [2010]

links.title: How to conduct a systematic or evidence-based literature review
links.description: Five-part author's guide to performing systematic reviews; illustrated, with examples. [2013]

links.title: Randomised controlled trials and population-based observational research
links.description: Reviews the distinct roles, occasional tensions, and relative strengths and limitations of RCTs versus population-based observational studies, proposed as complementary forms of research. [2014]

links.title: The statistical significance of randomized controlled trial results is frequently fragile: a case for a Fragility Index
links.description: Discusses how significant results of many RCTs hinge on very few events, and suggests that reporting the number of events required to make a statistically significant result nonsignificant (the Fragility Index) in RCTs can allow for more informed decisions about the confidence warranted by reported RCT results. [2014]

links.title: Teaching Critical Appraisal of Medical Evidence
links.description: Presents three practical methods for actively teaching critical appraisal skills in an evidence-based medicine curriculum. [2013]

links.title: R in Clinical Research
links.description: Presentation on the use of the R statistical package in Evidence-Based Medicine, especially in Clinical Research, intended mainly for, but not limited to, Bio-statisticians, especially those using SAS.

links.title: Evaluating the Evidence for evidence-based medicine: are randomized clinical trials less flawed than other forms of peer-reviewed medical research?
links.description: Critical review of RCT and non-RCT studies, finding that the implementation of RCT methods and the interpretation of the results can be flawed by poor trial design, observer bias, incentive bias, or simple misinterpretation. [2013]

links.title: Evidence-Based Practice: A Practice Manual
links.description: Details the basic steps of evidence-based practice and provides signposts to more detailed information and assistance. Compiled by the Evidence-Based Practice Group South East and the Health Service Executive of Ireland. [2014]

links.title: Evaluating Guidelines: A Review of Key Quality Criteria
links.description: A review of guideline-assessing instruments, finding that alongside the comprehensive instruments such as AGREE II and DELBI, rapid-assessment instruments can be convenient tools for gaining a quick impression of the value of a guideline. [2015]

links.title: Are randomized trials obsolete or more important than ever in the genomic era?
links.description: Given rapid development of new genomic biomarkers, this paper explores whether and how we can make randomized trials more adaptable to a changing landscape, and whether we still need such trials at all. [2013]

links.title: Adaptive clinical trial designs in oncology
links.description: Discusses the nature, types, and pros and cons of adaptive designs in oncology trials that use accumulating data to modify the ongoing trial without undermining the integrity and validity of the trial. [2014]

links.title: BMC Medicine | Full text |  Trustworthy guidelines – excellent; customized care tools –
links.description: Examination of how to develop trustworthy clinical practice guidelines that besides examining what is medically best also allow consistency with patients’ priorities, concerns, and preferences, thus delivering customized care at the level of individuals and their families. [2015]

links.title: Applying Evidence-Based Medicine in Actual Clinical Practice: Can We Bridge the Gap? A Review of the Literature

links.title: Research Trends in Evidence-Based Medicine: A Joinpoint Regression Analysis of More than 50 Years of Publication Data
links.description: A bibliometric analysis examing the scientific productivity of EBM research and publication trends over decades. [2015]

links.title: Proposal for Standardized Definitions for Efficacy End Points in Adjuvant Breast Cancer Trials: The STEEP System

links.title: Survival End Point Reporting in Randomized Cancer Clinical Trials: A Review of Major Journals
links.description: Evaluation of the reporting of survival end points in cancer RCTs. [2008]

links.title: Inconsistent selection and definition of local and regional endpoints in breast cancer research
links.description: Review of which locoregional endpoints are used in studies of breast cancer, and how these endpoints and their components are defined. [2014]

links.title: Use of Multiple Endpoints and Approval Paths Depicts a Decade of FDA Oncology Drug Approvals
links.description: Explores the historic use of different endpoints, and the associated degree of regulatory flexibility shown, by the FDA to support regular and accelerated approval of cancer drugs. [2013]

links.title: The random allocation process: two things you need to know
links.description: Describes the random allocation process, and the associated methods of allocation concealment. [2010]

links.title: Evidence-based medicine has been hijacked: a report to David Sackett
links.description: Reflections growing out of a conversation by John Ioannidis with David Sackett in 2004 about evidence-based medicine (EBM), the movement Sackett had spearheaded, updated to developments through 2016. [2016]

links.title: Randomization: beyond tossing a coin
links.description: A review of common randomization strategies, and how to choose betweeen them. [2016]

links.title: Mendelian randomization studies: a review of the approaches used and the quality of reporting
links.description: An overview of the methodological approaches used in Mendelian randomization studies, with a discussion of MR assumptions and reporting of statistical methods. and a checklist for the reporting of MR studies. [2015]

links.title: Mendelian randomization: where are we now and where are we going?

links.title: Clinical Research and Evidence-Based Medicine
links.description: A review of EBM principles, as well as how it is complemented by personalized medicine; precision medicine; and artificial intelligence and big data. [2019]

links.description: Evidence-based medicine (EBM) is defined as the integration of best research evidence with clinical expertise and patient values. This chapter describes the key principles of EBM and the process of...

links.title: GRADE: Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation

links.title: Systematic Reviews
links.description: Essentials of systematic reviews, and a step-by-step guide for how to conduct one. From Library Services of King's College, London. [2014]

links.title: The Added Value of Confidence Intervals

links.title: Assessing the Evidence in Evidence‐Based Medicine
links.description: A comprehensive critical examination and explication of the main tenets of evidence-based medicine. [2018]

links.title: Evidence Based Medicine (EBM)

links.description: Provides a summary of the principles, processes, and foundations of evidence-based decision making. Sample chapter from "Evidence-based Practice Across the Health Professions". [2013]

links.title: Introduction to Evidence-Based Medicine (EBM)
links.description: A five minute tutorial, with inbuilt self-assessment, from the Boston University Medical Library.

links.description: Compares and evaluates the optimum grading system (SIGN, GRADE, GATE and NSF-LTC) for the type of guideline being developed or question being addressed by a specialist society. [2010]

links.title: GRADE: an emerging consensus on rating quality of evidence and strength of recommendations
links.description: The advantages of the GRADE system for rating the quality of evidence and strength of recommendations.

[2015]

links.description: Evidence-based systematic reviews of interventions in stroke rehabilitation for clinicians; those with stroke and their families. Includes ratings of interventions and assessments with levels of evidence rating. Canadian-based.

links.title: Evidence-based guideline update: Pharmacologic treatment for episodic migraine prevention in adults
links.description: Updated evidence-based recommendations for the preventive treatment of migraine headache, from the American Academy of Neurology. [2013]

links.title: Evidence-based guideline: Treatment of tardive syndromes
links.description: Evidence-based recommendations regarding management of tardive syndromes (TDS), including tardive dyskinesias (TDD); from the American Academy of Neurology. [2013]

links.title: Guidelines for the Management of Cognitive and Behavioral Problems in Dementia
links.description: Evidence-based review of the effects of nonpharmacologic and pharmacologic interventions on the functional abilities and behavior of patients with dementia, and how these can be implemented into clinical practice. [2012]

links.title: Evidence-based guideline: Pharmacologic treatment of chorea in Huntington disease
links.description: Examines for adult patients with HD requiring symptomatic chorea therapy what available pharmacologic and non-pharmacologic (CoQ10) agents effectively reduce chorea as measured by validated scales. From the American Academy of Neurology. [2012]

links.title: Autism spectrum disorder: advances in evidence-based practice
links.description: Review of best practices for primary and clinical care of ASD based on high-level evidence only (from randomized controlled trials (RCTs) or systematic reviews), covering its etiology, diagnosis and treatment. [2014]

links.title: Practical Diagnosis and Management of Dementia Due to Alzheimer’s Disease in the Primary Care Setting: An Evidence-Based Approach
links.description: Evidence-based guidance on the primary care of Alzheimer’s disease, including cognitive assessment, diagnosis and management. [2013]

links.title: Autism spectrum disorder: advances in evidence-based practice
links.description: Outlines the current understanding of ASD and suggest best practices for primary care and specialized clinics based on evidence (when availablke) from randomized controlled trials (RCTs) or systematic reviews. [2014]

links.title: Evidence-based guidelines for the pharmacological management of attention deficit hyperactivity disorder
links.description: A review of recent research in the fields of neuroimaging, neuropsychology and genetics of ADHD, representing an update on recommendations from the British Association for Psychopharmacology (BAP) through 2014.

links.title: Evidence-Based Neurocritical Care
links.description: Evidence-based review of the landmark studies on the treatment and management of patients with life-threatening neurological illnesses, postoperative neurosurgical complications, and neurological manifestations of systemic disease. [2014]

links.title: Complementary and Alternative Treatments for Autism Part 1: Evidence-Supported Treatments, Apr 15 -
links.description: Discusses the bioethics issues surrounding using evidence that some complementary and alternative treatments improve physiological abnormalities in autism, From the AMA Journal of Ethics. [2015]

links.title: Complementary and Alternative Treatments for Autism Part 2: Identifying and Avoiding Non-Evidence-Ba
links.description: Discusses the bioethics issues surrounding using evidence from complementary and alternative treatments for autism, advising only robust evidence-based interventions. From the AMA Journal of Ethics. [2015]

links.title: Changing practice in dementia care in the community: developing and testing evidence-based interventions, from timely diagnosis to end of life (EVIDEM)
links.description: An evidence-based, mixed-methodologies, program of interdisciplinarity collaboration in dementia research from diagnosis through to end-of-life care. [2015]

links.title: Evidence-Based Treatments for Autism Spectrum Disorder
links.description: An overview of current treatment options for the management of both core ASD symptoms and clinical features, including pharmacological, dietary, lifestyle, physical, behavorial, educational, psychosocial, and complementary and alternative medicine (CAM) interventions. [2015]

links.title: Interventions for Attention-Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder: A Year in Review
links.description: Up-to-date summary and critical analysis of both new and well-established ADHD interventions during 2014. [2015]

links.title: Diagnosing Mild Cognitive Impairment (MCI) in clinical trials: a systematic review
links.description: Evidence-based review that documents the lack of uniformity in clinical diagnosis of MCI, considered by some an intermediate state between normal ageing and dementia, as well for Alzheimer's disease and predementia, and argues for a uniform approach to MCI classification, and for any classification concept within the field of dementia. [2013]

links.title: Effect of Physical Exercise on Cognitive Performance in Older Adults with Mild Cognitive Impairment or Dementia: A Systematic Review
links.description: Systematically reviews the evidence from 22 randomized controlled trials (RCTs) on the effects of physical exercise on cognition in older subjects with either MCI or dementia, with some positive effects on cognition found in studies on older subjects with MCI. [2014]

links.title: Association of Mediterranean diet with Mild Cognitive Impairment and Alzheimer’s disease: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
links.description: Reviews the association between the Mediterranean diet and cognitive impairment, finding higher adherence to the diet to be associated with a reduced risk of developing both MCI and Alzheimer's Disease, as well as a reduced risk of progressing from MCI to Alzheimer's. [2014]

links.title: Role of Environmental Contaminants in the Etiology of Alzheimer's Disease: A Review
links.description: Reviews in vitro, animal and epidemiological studies on the etiology of Alzheimer's Disease, highlighting evidence supportive of the link between toxic environmental exposures and the development of Alzheimer's pathology. [2015]

links.title: Is Transient Ischemic Attack a Medical Emergency? An Evidence-Based Analysis
links.description: Systematic review investigating the impact of the urgent evaluation and initiation of treatment of patients with TIA on the risk of subsequent stroke and death. From the Ontario Health Technology Assessment Series. [2015]

links.title: Optimizing therapy early in multiple sclerosis: An evidence-based view
links.description: An overview of the efficacy of disease-modifying therapies on conventional MS outcome measures, in order to prevent prevent the accumulation of irreversible neurological damage and reduce the risk of disease progression. [2015]

links.title: Acupuncture for Pain Management in Evidence-based Medicine
links.description: Review of high-level evidence from RCTs and meta-analyses of the effectiveness of acupuncture in the management of pain. [2015]

links.title: Evidence-based treatments for cluster headache
links.description: A review of the pathogenesis of cluster headaches and the evidence supporting the most promising treatment options. [2015]

links.title: Evidence-Based Treatments for Adults with Migraine
links.description: Reviews the options for the acute and prophylactic management of migraine, both pharmacological, as well as invasive and noninvasive treatments, including neuromodulation. [2015]

links.title: Mild cognitive decline. A position statement of the Cognitive Decline Group of the European Innovation Partnership for Active and Healthy Ageing (EIPAHA)
links.description: Critical appraisal of the evidence on the definition, prevalence and stability, risk factors, screening, and management and intervention of mild cognitive impairment (MCI). [2016]

links.title: Switching and stopping antidepressants | Issue 3 | Volume 39 | Australian Prescriber
links.description: Review of strategies for switching antidepressants, including drug cessation versus gradual antidepressant withdrawal, and the issue of drug washout periods. [2016]

links.title: Evidence-based Approaches to Preventing Alzheimer’s Disease, Part 1
links.description: An evidence-based review of the modifiable risk factors of Alzheimer's Disease, especially vascular, and including dietary factors. [2009]

452677.title: Obstetrics and Gynecology
452677.description: For sites concerning the application of EBM principles to the practice of Obstetrics and/or Gynecology.

links.title: SaPeRiDoc
links.description: Resources for professionals and women on perinatal, reproductive and sexual health. Italian and English.

links.title: RCOG: National Evidence-Based Clinical Guidelines
links.description: A list of publications from the Royal College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists, including date of next review. Many can be downloaded as PDF files.

links.title: Evidence-based Obstetrics & Gynecology
links.description: A quarterly  journal with review articles and expert commentary. Includes table of contents and details of subscription.

links.title: An Evidence-Based Approach to Determining Route of Delivery for Twin Gestations
links.description: Review and guidance on best methods of delivery for minimizing the major complications and high perinatal mortality associated with prematurity of preterm twins. [2011]

links.title: Evidence-Based Medicine: An Obstetrician and Gynaecologist’s Perspective
links.description: Discussion of what ‘Evidence-based Obstetrics and Gynaecology’ exactly is, why is it required, for whom is it meant and how is to be practiced and propagated. [2012]

links.title: Prescribing menopausal hormone therapy: an evidence-based approach
links.description: A litertaure review clarifying the balance of benefits and risks for hormone therapy use in postmenopausal women, and offering evidence-based recommendations in the wake of the WHI (Women's Health Initiative) study. Available as downloadable PDF. [2014]

links.title: Evidence based surgical management of endometriosis
links.description: Review of surgical strategies and the management of endometriosis, with an emphasis on pain and fertility outcomes. [2012]

links.title: Evidence-based reproductive medicine: a critical appraisal
links.description: Appraisal of the evidence from meta-analyses and systematic reviews on two critical problems in in vitro fertilization: (1) failed implantation and (2) poor ovarian response to ovarian stimulation. [2013]

links.title: RCOG: National Evidence-Based Clinical Guidelines
links.description: A list of publications from the Royal College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists, including date of next review. Many can be downloaded as PDF files.

links.title: Evidence-based management of recurrent miscarriages
links.description: Evidence-based guidance on clinical management of recurrent miscarriage. [2014]

links.title: SOGC: Clinical Practice Guidelines
links.description: The Society of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists of Canada presents a list of PDF evidence-based guidelines for OB/GYN and related subspecialties.

452696.title: Occupational Medicine
452696.description: For sites concerning the application of EBM principles to the practice of Occupational Medicine.

links.title: OTseeker
links.description: Database of abstracts of systematic reviews, randomized controlled trials, and critical appraisals in occupational therapy. With detailed EBM tutorial.

links.title: PEDro
links.description: A project of the Centre of Evidence-Based Physiotherapy (Cochrane Collaboration), this is a searchable database of randomized controlled trials, systematic reviews and practice guidelines in physiotherapy.

links.title: ACOEM - Evidence Based Statements: Occupational & Environmental Medicine
links.description: Guidelines in OEM (occupational and environmental medicine).

links.title: Evidence-based guidelines: occupational contact dermatitis and urticaria
links.description: Critical discussion of available systematic reviews on occupational contact dermatitis, especially that from the British Occupational Health Research Foundation (BOHRF). [2010]

links.title: Bronchial asthma and COPD due to irritants in the workplace - an evidence-based approach
links.description: Overview of the evidence related to irritative agents causing occupational asthma or occupational COPD. [2013]

links.title: A compendium of causative agents of occupational asthma
links.description: An evidence-based assessment and compendium of allergenic and irritant agents known to cause occupational asthma, with the goal of improving diagnostics and disease management. [2013]

links.title: Effectiveness of occupation-based interventions to improve areas of occupation and social participation after stroke: an evidence-based review
links.description: A systematic review identifying, evaluating, and synthesizing the evidence for the effectiveness of post-stroke activity- and occupation-based interventions for improving areas of occupation and social participation. [2015]

links.title: Asthma in the workplace: a case-based discussion and review of current evidence
links.description: Explores and reviews the evidence for the relationship between asthma and the workplace in the form of a clinical practice scenario with real-time commentary about management decisions in evidence-based practice. [2013]

links.title: Evidence based medicine in physical medicine and rehabilitation
links.description: Exploration of the significance of evidence-based medicine in physical medicine and general rehabilitation. [2013]

links.title: Evidence Based Practice - Physical Therapy
links.description: EBM resources from the World Confederation for Physical Therapy.

links.title: Concise guidance: diagnosis, management and prevention of occupational asthma
links.description: Guideline for the prevention, identification and management of occupational asthma, from the British Occupational Health Research Foundation (BOHRF). [2012]

452689.title: Oncology
452689.description: For sites concerning the application of EBM principles to the practice of Oncology.

links.title: Oncologystat
links.description: Evidence-based oncology news, research, education, and analysis, with some free full-text access to peer-reviewed content.

links.title: NCCN Guidelines for Patients
links.description: Patient versions of authoritative NCCN guidelines for the treatment of nine of the most common cancer types. From The National Comprehensive Cancer Network (NCCN), a not-for-profit alliance of leading cancer centers in the U.S.

links.title: Clinical Practice Guidelines in Oncology
links.description: Evidence-based guidelines and consensus statements from the New Zealand Ministry of Health (MOH), downloadable as PDFs.

links.title: Diagnosis and Management of Lung Cancer: ACCP Evidence-Based Guidelines
links.description: Lung cancer guidelines from the American College of Chest Physicians (ACCP).

links.title: Eight ways to stay healthy after cancer: an evidence-based message
links.description: A message campaign that provides cancer survivors with an evidence-based, but user-friendly, approach detailing eight domains of a critical health promotion program. [2013]

links.title: HemOnc.org
links.description: A collaborative wiki created by oncologists as a knowledge base for oncotherapy (chemotherapy, biological, and endocrine) drugs and regimens subcategorized by cancer type, providing dosing, schedule and level of confirming evidence.

links.title: Hepatocellular carcinoma review: Current treatment, and evidence-based medicine
links.description: An overview of treatment of early and advanced stage hepatocellular carcinoma based on extensive literature review. [2014]

links.title: Quality of Reporting of Modern Randomized Controlled Trials in Medical Oncology: A Systematic Review
links.description: Assesses the overall reporting quality of oncology RCTs according to recognized CONSORT criteria, finding that despite significant improvments, many items remain very poorly reported and may conceal important problems in trial design or conduct. [2012]

links.title: Adherence to CONSORT Adverse Event Reporting Guidelines in Randomized Clinical Trials Evaluating Systemic Cancer Therapy: A Systematic Review
links.description: Review that finds poor reporting of adverse events (AEs) in oncology RCTs, which was not appreciably better among articles published in high impact factor journals. [2013]

links.title: ASH Clinical Guidelines
links.description: Oncology-oriented evidence-based practice guidelines, from American Society of Hematology (ASH).

links.title: Clinical best practice
links.description: Evidence-based clinical practice guidelines, guides and recommendations for various cancer types, from Cancer Australia.

links.title: Locoregional therapy of locally advanced breast cancer: a clinical practice guideline | Brackstone |
links.description: Systematic review supporting key therapeutic recommendations for locally advanced breast cancer (LABC), from Cancer Care Ontario's Program in Evidence-Based Care and the Breast Cancer Disease Site Group. [2015]

links.title: Evidence-based Clinical Practice Guidelines for Interventional Pain Management in Cancer Pain
links.description: Evidence-based practice guidelines for interventional therapies in the management of iintractable cancer pain not amenable to standard oral or parenteral analgesics. [2015]

links.title: Complementary Therapies and Integrative Medicine in Lung Cancer: Diagnosis and Management of Lung Cancer, 3rd ed: American College of Chest Physicians Evidence-Based Clinical Practice Guidelines
links.description: Systematic review of randomized controlled trials, systematic reviews, meta-analyses, and prospective cohort studies assessing the current evidence base on the benefits and risks of complementary therapies in patients with lung cancer. [2013]

links.title: Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Use of Integrative Therapies as Supportive Care in Patients Treated for Breast Cancer
links.description: Evidence-based clinical practice guidelines for the use of complementary and/or integrative therapies in breast cancer patients during and beyond cancer treatment to manage symptoms, prevent toxicities, and improve quality of life; Journal of the National Cancer Institute Monograph. [2014]

links.title: Diabetes and cancer: A critical appraisal of the pathogenetic and therapeutic links
links.description: Summarizes the epidemiological evidence for an association between diabetes and various cancers, and explores the pathophysiological mechanisms potentially involved in promoting carcinogenesis in diabetes and the impact of different anti-diabetic therapies on cancer risk. [2015]

links.title: Prostate-Specific Antigen Screening in Prostate Cancer: Perspectives on the Evidence
links.description: Discusses and contrasts two perspectives on the evidence for PSA screening from opposing camps on this issue: Dr Timothy Wilt on the hazards of PSA screening and Dr Peter Scardino on the merits of tailored PSA screening. From an educational session at the 2013 ASCO annual meeting on this topic. [2014]

links.title: Rectal cancer: An evidence-based update for primary care providers
links.description: Overview of the diagnosis, staging and multimodal therapy in primary care of patients with rectal cancer. [2015]

links.title: Outcome analysis of breast cancer patients who declined evidence-based treatment
links.description: Exploration of the characteristics and survival outcomes of women with breast cancer who declined recommended primary standard treatments. [2012]

links.title: Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Use of Integrative Therapies as Supportive Care in Patients Trea
links.description: A systematic review based on the Institute of Medicine’s guideline development process to identify randomized controlled trials on the efficacy of integrative therapies for supportive care in patients receiving breast cancer treatment. [2014]

links.title: Building the Evidence Base for Integrative Approaches to Care of Cancer Survivors
links.description: Appreciation of the work and goals of the National Center for Complementary and Alternative Medicine (NCCAM) of the National Institutes of Health (NIH) in assessing efficacy and safety of interventions in integrative oncology. [2014]

links.title: Medical marijuana for cancer
links.description: Evidence-based review the literature on the medical use and safety of marijuana and cannabinoid pharmaceuticals, with emphasis on indications relevant to oncology. [2015]

links.title: Mind-Body Practices in Cancer Care
links.description: Evidence-based review from MD Anderson Cancer Center of mind-body techniques such as meditation, yoga, tai chi, and qigong for improvements in different aspects of the quality of life of cancer patients. [2015]

links.title: Cancer and fertility preservation: international recommendations from an expert meeting
links.description: Ten recommendations to help physicians in counseling their young cancer patients interested in fertility preservation, from a workshop of content experts on the topic of “cancer and fertility preservation” held in Genova in April 2015. [2016]

links.title: Review complementary and integrative interventions for cancer-related cognitive changes
links.description: Review of existing evidence for the use of complementary and integrative interventions to prevent or treat cancer-related cognitive changes and discussion of the rationale for current and future research. [2015]

links.title: Early Detection of Anthracycline Cardiotoxicity and Improvement With Heart Failure Therapy
links.description: Prospective evaluation of the incidence, time of occurrence, clinical correlates, and response to heart failure therapy of anthracycline-related cardiotoxicity in the oncology setting. [2015]

links.title: Illuminating anthracycline cardiotoxicity: the renaissance of evidence-based onco-cardiology
links.description: Reflections on, and an editorial call for, a transition of onco-cardiology from an expert-based into an evidence-based discipline. Article in Journal of Thoracic Disease [2015]

links.title: Anthracycline Cardiotoxicity - A New Paradigm for an Old Classic
links.description: Reflections on the problem of cardiotoxicity in cardio-oncology, the current state-of-the-art, and what needs to still be achieved. [2015]

links.title: Hepatocellular carcinoma: From clinical practice to evidence-based treatment protocols
links.description: Critical review of the best evidence to date for the treatment of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), both local therapies and pharmacological interventions. [2015]

links.title: Vitamin D and Its Relationship with Breast Cancer: An Evidence Based Practice Paper
links.description: Evaluation of the relationship between vitamin D levels and breast cancer risk. [2015]

links.title: Review of hormone-based treatments in postmenopausal patients with advanced breast cancer focusing on aromatase inhibitors and fulvestrant
links.description: Critical evaluation of outcome in clinical trials performed in postmenopausal patients with advanced breast cancer treated with various endocrine regimens, including letrozole, anastrozole, exemestane and fulvestrant. [2016]

links.title: Cancer Guidelines Database
links.description: A searchable database of more than 1,000 English-language cancer control guidelines and standards released, rated for reporting quality using the AGREE II assessment tool. From the Canadian Partnership Against Cancer.

links.title: SIO Clinical Practice Guidelines
links.description: Collection of cancer-specific guidelines from the Society of Surgical Oncology (SIO).

links.title: Breast Cancer Screening and Diagnosis: A Synopsis of the European Breast Guidelines
links.description: Summary of key recommendations from the European Breast Guidelines, based on evidence aggregated from 2016 to 2018. [2020]

links.title: ASCO Clinical Practice Guidelines
links.description: Authoritative clinical practice guidelines for oncology professionals, including treatment and supportive care, and assays and predictive markers. From the American Society of Clinical Oncology whose guidelines, along with those of NCCN, determine current oncology practice.

links.title: ESMO Clinical Practice Guidelines
links.description: Evidence-based recommendations for the best standards of cancer care. From the European Society for Medical Oncology (ESMO).

links.title: PEBC: Program in Evidence-based Care
links.description: Evidence-based systematic reviews in cancer care and research, with evidence summaries for both healthcare providers and the public. From Cancer Care ontario.

links.title: NCCN Clinical Practice Guidelines in Oncology
links.description: Authoritative guidelines for oncology professionals for the treatment of all major malignancies, and for their detection, prevention, risk reduction, and associated supportive care. From The National Comprehensive Cancer Network (NCCN), a not-for-profit alliance of leading cancer centers in the U.S.

links.title: Speeding the Dissemination and Implementation of Evidence-Based Interventions for Cancer Control and Prevention
links.description: Describes interactive approaches for accelerating dissemination and implementation of evidence-based interventions in oncology, illustrated using examples from obesity prevention and tobacco control. [2014]

452690.title: Opposing Views
452690.description: Evidence-based medicine and its methodology, although now widely accepted, is still the subject of considerable critical assessment and debate, and the entries in this subcategory are intended to represent the broad range of critical assessment and appreciation of EBM from a number of perspectives.

links.title: Deconstructing the evidence-based discourse in health sciences: truth, power and fascism
links.description: The article that initiated the critical controversy surrounding the claim that EBM represents an exclusionary "regime of power".

links.title: Evidence-based medicine: a commentary on common criticisms
links.description: Review of the most commonly leveled charges against, and misperceptions about, evidence-based medicine, with proposed solutions to real limitations.

links.title: The case against 'the evidence': a different perspective on evidence-based medicine
links.description: A psychiatrist's critique that over-emphasis on evidence-based medicine oversimplifies the complex and interpersonal nature of clinical care.

links.title: The pragmatic randomised controlled trial
links.description: A critique of conventional randomized controlled trials methodology, and an attempt to incorporate more complex interventions via a new 'pragmatic RCT'.

links.title: Is Evidence-Based Medicine Relevant to the Developing World?
links.description: Argues and discusses the reasons for the limited relevance of systematic reviews to frontline health care workers in developing countries. [2005]

links.title: A philosophical analysis of the evidence-based medicine debate
links.description: A review of criticisms of EBM as being founded on a lack of clarity and precision by EBM's own proponents.

links.title: False dichotomies: EBM, clinical freedom, and the art of medicine
links.description: A critical evaluation of the oft-cited criticism of evidence-based medicine as constraining clinical freedom and potentially compromising patient welfare. Published: 03/01/05. [Requires registration.]

links.title: Point: Evidence-Based Medicine Has a Sound Scientific Base
links.description: A defense of evidence-based medicine as an evolving and highly individualized, patient-centered approach to clinical decision making. Part of a Point/Counterpoint exchange on EBM from the Chest journal. [2008]

links.title: Counterpoint: Evidence-Based Medicine Lacks a Sound Scientific Base
links.description: A critique of evidence-based medicine, especially its EBM-grading construct, as scientifically unsound. Part of a Point/Counterpoint exchange on EBM from the Chest journal. [2008]

links.title: Evidence-Based Medicine: Haute Couture or the Emperor's New Clothes?
links.description: An examination of some strengths and weaknesses of evidence-based medicine as it relates to the practice of anesthesiology.

links.title: The Evidence-based Medicine Paradigm: Where are We 20 Years Later? Part 1
links.description: Critical review of progress in, and limitations, of evidence-based medcine methodology over the two decades since inception. [2013]

links.title: The Evidence-based Medicine Paradigm: Where are We 20 Years Later? Part 2
links.description: Critical review of progress in, and limitations, of evidence-based medcine over the two decades since inception. [2013]

links.title: Evidence-based medicine - are we boiling the frog?
links.description: Presents some limitations of EBM, especially the mistaking of statistical significance with clinical significance / relevance. [2013]

links.title: Evidence-Based Medicine: Examining the Gap Between Rhetoric and Reality
links.description: A plea for a more thoughtful and critical re-examination of evidence-based medicine as it relates to optimal and personalized cancer management. [2013]

links.title: Evidence based medicine: Can everything be evident?
Evidence based medicine—older, but no better educated?
links.description: A follow-up, 15 years hence (2010), of the lanmark audit in 1995, of the extent to which general medical inpatients were managed in an evidence-based manner in a large tertiary teaching hospital,. [2013]

links.title: Evidence based medicine: a movement in crisis?
links.description: Argues that although evidence based medicine has had many benefits, it has also had some negative unintended consequences; the authors provide some constructive suggestions for addressing these concerns and limitations. [2014]

links.title: How evidence-based medicine is failing due to biased trials and selective publication
links.description: A sustained critique of evidence-based medicine's lack of independence given its high degree of industry-sponsored studies, but also offering some constructive suggestions for potential solutions. [2014]

links.title: Trials | Full text |  Randomised trials in context: practical problems and social aspects of evidenc
links.description: Critical examination of four important ways in which the evidence from randomised trials is limited or partial, that are claimed to undermine the evidence that such trials provide for decision-making. [2015]

links.title: Bright and dark sides of evidence-based  medicine
links.description: A review of the most common shortcomings of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) as used in evidence-based medicine, with particular focus on publication bias. [2016]

links.title: Evidence-based medicine: can the evidence be trusted?
links.description: Explores the problem of untrustworthy evidence, its sources and impact on quality in evidence-based medicine. [2011]

links.title: Criticisms of evidence-based medicine
links.description: Brief review of five major types of criticisms of EBM.

links.title: A categorization and analysis of the criticisms of Evidence-Based Medicine
links.description: An examination and assessment of a decade of critiques of EBM, categorized into five major themes. [2004]

links.title: Why Evidence-Based Medicine Cannot Be Applied to Psychiatry
links.description: Argues that there is insufficient proof that the EBM model can be adapted to fit psychiatry. (April 1, 2008).

links.title: Evidence‐poor medicine: just how evidence‐based are Australian clinical practice guidelines?
links.description: From a review of 748 graded recommendations in Australian guidelines, only 18% were found to be based on Level I evidence, suggesting that contemporary medicine appears to remain largely evidence‐poor, not evidence‐based. [2020]

links.title: Filling the glass of evidence‐based medicine
links.description: An editorial about the seminal article "Evidence‐poor medicine" (Venus & Jamrozik), that disputes the claim that most guideline recommendations are not evidence-based. [2020]

links.title: The Real World Failure of Evidence-Based Medicine
links.description: Argues that EBM is an ad hoc construct and not a valid basis for medical decision-making. [2011]

452694.title: Pathology
452694.description: For sites concerning the application of EBM principles to the practice of Pathology.

links.title: Original research in pathology: judgment, or evidence-based medicine?
links.description: Examines whether the practice of anatomic pathology fulfills the tenets of evidence-based medicine (EBM), arguing that anatomic pathology has in fact a unique place in the practice of EBM.

links.title: Evidence-Based Principles in Pathology: Existing Problem Areas and the Development of “Quality” Practice Patterns
links.description: Asks the question "Are pathologists, in fact, as evidence based as they believe?", showing large areas of both anatomic and clinical pathology where evidence-based methodologies have not been applied, and offering constructive suggestions for more systematic application.

links.title: Evidence-based pathology and the pathologic evaluation of thymomas
links.description: Documents the lack of randomized clinical trials evaluating the prognosis of patients with thymomas and the effects of various treatment modalities, and calls for an international cooperative study and meta-analysis of thymomas. [2008]

links.title: Evidence Levels for Publications in Pathology and Laboratory Medicine
links.description: Discussion of the inadequacies of current schemes for the evaluation of evidence levels, along with a proposed scale of evidence levels for more appropriate to publications in pathology. [2011]

links.title: Application of GRADE: Making Evidence-Based Recommendations about diagnostic tests in clinical practice guidelines
links.description: Analysis of requirements for clinical practice guidelines in order to facilitate implementation and strengthen confidence in recommendations about diagnostic tests. [2011]

links.title: American Society of Clinical Oncology/College of American Pathologists Guideline Recommendations for Immunohistochemical Testing of Estrogen and Progesterone Receptors in Breast Cancer
links.description: ASCO Guideline on how to improve the accuracy of ER and PR testing in breast cancer and on the utility of these receptors as predictive markers. [2010]

links.title: Evidence-Based Pathology: Systematic Literature Reviews as the Basis for Guidelines and Best Practices
links.description: Review of the history and basic concepts of evidence-based medicine and evidence-based pathology, and how to perform and interpret systematic reviews, and integrate best evidence into guidelines. [2015]

links.title: Evidence-Based Pathology: Systematic Literature Reviews as the Basis for Guidelines and Best Practices
links.description: Reviews history and basic concepts of evidence-based medicine and evidence-based pathology, how to perform and interpret systematic reviews, and how to integrate best evidence into guidelines. [2015]

links.title: Evidence-Based Pathology and the Pathologic Evaluation of Thymomas: Transcapsular Invasion Is Not a Significant Prognostic Feature
links.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis of the prognostic importance of transcapsular invasion in thymoma stage I and II, finding it not a significant prognostic feature of any clinical value. [2008]

452688.title: Pediatrics
452688.description: For sites concerning the application of EBM principles to the practice of Pediatrics.

links.title: Centre for Evidence-Based Child Health
links.description: Providing an educational programme for health professionals, with tutorial notes and a list of publications. Associated with Great Ormond Street Hospital in the United Kingdom.

links.title: Evidence-Based Clinical Practice Guidelines
links.description: The Cincinnati Children's Hospital Medical Center provides a list of publications available for download as PDF files.

links.title: Management of Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus in Children and Adolescents
links.description: Evidence-based clinical practice guidelines on the management of diabetic patients between 10 and 18 years of age, for treatment of both primary disease and comorbidities. From the American Academy of Pediatrics. [2013]

links.title: Academy of Nutrition and Dietetics Evidence Analysis Library (EAL)
links.description: The Evidence Analysis Library is a synthesis of the best, most relevant nutritional research on important dietetic practice questions, housing systematic reviews and practice guidelines related to the topics of food and nutrition.

links.title: The Journal of Pediatrics Current Best Evidence
links.description: Collection of concise summaries of the best evidence in pediatrics, along with commentaries from experts to put this evidence into context.

links.title: UM Evidence-Based Pediatrics Web Site
links.description: Resources for the practice of evidence-based pediatrics, including a pediatric journal club and a series of critically-appraised topics. From the University of Michigan.

links.title: PedsCCM Evidence-Based Journal Club
links.description: Peer-reviewed evidence-based critical assessments of clinical trials in pediatric critical care, with EBM resource links.

links.title: AAP Practice Guidelines
links.description: Evidence-based decision-making clinical guidelines for managing common pediatric conditions, from the American Academy of Pediatrics (AAP).

links.title: Vaccine Safety: Examine the Evidence
links.description: Critical review of central studies on the claimed association between vaccines and autism in children, showing the claims to lack evidential support. From the American Academy of Pediatrics (AAP). [2018]

452683.title: Psychiatry
452683.description: For sites concerning the application of EBM principles to the practice of Psychiatry.

links.title: KlinPsy - Evidence Based Psychology
links.description: Belgium-based collection of EBM resources (most in English language) in Psychology and Mental Health.

links.title: The Clinical Management of Bipolar Disorder: A Review of Evidence-Based Guidelines
links.description: Reviews the diagnostic criteria, differential diagnosis, and the current evidence-based treatments of bipolar disorders. [2011]

453463.description: ...Informatics is an emerging discipline that has been defined as the study, invention, and implementation of structures and algorithms to improve communication, understanding and management of medical information. The focus on the structures and algorithms necessary to manipulate the information separates Biomedical Informatics from other medical disciplines where information content is the focus."                  Aamir M. Zakaria., MD           "Medical Informatics Frequently Asked Questions"

"An Electronic Health Record Architectures (EHRA) is an information model or framework for the construction of  electronic health records. It has been defined by the European Standards Committee (CEN). An EHR Architecture is a model of the generic features necessary in any electronic healthcare record in order that the record may be communicable, complete, a useful and effective ethico-legal record of care, and may retain integrity  across systems, countries, and time. The Architecture does not prescribe or dictate what anyone stores in their healthcare records. Nor does it prescribe or dictate how  any electronic healthcare record system is implemented. It places no restrictions on the types of data which can appear in the record, including those which have no  counterpart in paper records."  From http://www.gehr.org/gpcgglossary.pdf Viewed 22/12/2003

453465.title: Health Level 7
453465.description: Health Level Seven is one of several ANSI-accredited Standards Developing Organizations (SDOs) operating in the healthcare arena. Most SDOs produce standards (sometimes called specifications or protocols) for a particular healthcare domain such as pharmacy, medical devices, imaging or insurance (claims processing) transactions. Health Level Seven's domain is clinical and administrative data. Our mission is to: "To provide standards for the exchange, management and integration of data that support clinical patient care and the management, delivery and evaluation of healthcare services. Specifically, to create flexible, cost effective approaches, standards, guidelines, methodologies, and related services for interoperability between healthcare information systems."    "Level Seven" refers to the highest level of the International Standards Organization's (ISO) communications model for Open Systems Interconnection (OSI) - the application level. The application level addresses definition of the data to be exchanged, the timing of the interchange, and the communication of certain errors to the application. The seventh level supports such functions as security checks, participant identification, availability checks, exchange mechanism negotiations and, most importantly, data exchange structuring.     The Reference Information Model (RIM) is the cornerstone of the HL7 Version 3 development process. An object model created as part of the Version 3 methodology, the RIM is a large pictorial representation of the clinical data (domains) and identifies the life cycle of events that a message or groups of related messages will carry. It is a shared model between all the domains and as such is the model from which all domains create their messages. Explicitly representing the connections that exist between the information carried in the fields of HL7 messages, the RIM is essential to our ongoing mission of increasing precision and reducing implementation costs.    Source - http://www.hl7.org/ Viewed on 18/12/2003

453179.title: Behavioral Medicine
453179.description: Behavior is a major factor in health and quality of life. Exercise, smoking, diet, ways of handling stress, are all behaviors, and all have huge impacts on health; to promote or damage health.  Behavioral medicine uses training, biofeedback, and self-management to treat diseases and to develop healthy behaviors.  An emphasis of behavioral medicine is putting the individual in control, by showing how to get control of your own behavior. An additional area of research and treatment: the connection between individual attitude and the immune system. You can actually improve your immune system by improving how you deal with and feel about your life.

453117.title: Critical Care
453117.description:
Critical care evolved from an historical recognition that the needs of patients with acute, life-threatening illness or injury could be better treated if they were grouped into specific areas of the hospital. Thus evolved the ICU, Intensive Care Units.

Care in these ICU's is provided by multidisciplinary teams of health care professionals who are organized by a qualified critical care physician. These physicians (intensivists) specialize in total patient care and understand the effects of treatments on each organ system in the body.

453358.title: Radiotherapy
453358.description: Radiotherapy is the use of radiation to treat conditions such as cancer. The most common technique exposes tumors to high energy photons (x-rays) and/or electrons while sparing normal tissues. Other uses are to prepare a patient for organ transplantation by suppressing immune response and to calm muscle twitches. The therapy can be delivered from the outside (external beam radiotherapy), by radioactive implants placed in the body (brachytherapy), or during surgery (interoperative). Other types of radiotherapy such as proton therapy and neutron therapy -- available at very limited centers -- have their own distinct advantages and disadvantages.

Chronic pain is a condition which persists for one to three months beyond the time that an expected acute pain or acute injury should subside or is associated with a chronic pathological process.  Pain management can be defined as the combination of various psychological techniques and practical strategies designed to optimize physical function, quality of life and to reduce emotional distress for people suffering with the effects of chronic pain. 452989.description:
This is a subspecialty of obstetrics and neonatology concerned with the care of the mother and fetus when there are increased risks of complications. Definitions vary, but the perinatal period begins approximately after 25th week of pregnancy and ends in the first month after birth.

A high-risk baby might be cared for by a perinatologist before and during birth, and by a neonatologist after birth, although at the time of delivery, both specialists are likely to be in attendance.

452345.title: Impotence
452345.description:
Impotence, or more properly Erectile Dysfunction (ED) is the inability to have an erection that is rigid enough or to maintain it long enough to complete sexual intercourse. Three other conditions can cause an inability to complete sexual union:
  • Peyronie's Disease, in which scar tissue or plaque forms on the shaft of the penis causing it to bend at an acute angle. In extreme cases, this can result in an inability to penetrate even though an erection is present, and the erection can be very painful.
  • Phimosis, a condition in uncircumcised men in which the foreskin, or prepuce, cannot be retracted from the head of the penis. This can cause painful erections and attendant impotence.
  • Premature Ejaculation, is characterized by ejaculation either before or soon after penetration. Its causes can be either psychological or physical.
This topic is dedicated to helping men and their partners become informed on what Erectile Dysfunction is, what causes it, and what can be done about it. ED IS CURABLE in almost all cases. There are many treatment options in existence, and many more are under development. Visit the links and become informed about the problem.

452009.title: Sensory Integration
452009.description: Sensory Integration is an interruption in the ability to assimilate our senses into our learning environment. Children may exhibit overly sensitive reactions to noises, touch, taste, smells, and sight.  Sensory Integration therapy has proven to be successful with children who are tactile defensive.   Some mental health clients have special issues that are barriers to productive work with a therapist.  Many of these barriers have to do with sensory overload or sensory deprivation.     For example, a person with oral sensory overload may not be able to handle eating and drinking without a great deal of stress and panic.  If that person becomes anorexia, for instance, the first step may be therapy to reduce the oral sensory overload, to bring down the stress and panic level of eating.

Sites which offer counseling services for people suffering from grief, loss, or bereavement.

Grief is the pain, misery, anguish, suffering, or distress caused by bereavement.

Loss occurs as a result of losing a possession, a person, or can be caused by deprivation or a change of circumstance. Losses can occur through the death of a child, a spouse, a friend, hero, leader, or relative.

Bereavement is caused by loss, especially the loss of a loved one. A loss of position in the community, dignity, security, or reputation can result in feelings of bereavement.

452079.title: Anxiety
452079.description: Anxiety has been defined as a feeling of fear, dread, or apprehension that arises without a clear or appropriate real-life justification. Some authorities differentiate anxiety from true fear in that the latter is experienced in response to an actual threat or danger, such as those to one's physical safety. Anxiety, on the other hand, may arise in response to apparently innocuous situations, or may be out of proportion to the actual degree of the external stress.  Generally, intense, persistent, or chronic anxiety that is not justified in response to real-life stresses, and that interferes with the individual's functioning, is regarded as a manifestation of mental disorder.   Anxiety is a symptom in many mental disorders, including schizophrenia, obsessive-compulsive disorders, post-traumatic stress disorders, and so on, but in phobias and other anxiety disorders proper, anxiety is the primary (and frequently the only) symptom.   Panic disorder (PD) is a common condition, the cardinal features of which are attacks of unexpected, severe anxiety, accompanied by physical symptoms like palpitations, a choking sensation, tingling, dizziness, and fear of dying or "going crazy".

452265.title: ADD and ADHD
452265.description:
Attention deficit disorder and attention deficit hyperactivity disorder are neuroldevelopmental conditions. Research indicates that problems producing neurotransmitters in the frontal lobe and limbic portions of the brain may be the cause.

Behaviors include distractibility, lack of impulse control, problems with organizing or sequencing tasks, restlessness, and forgetfulness.

links.title: Outside the Box - Helping Misunderstood Kids

links.title: Teaching the ADD Child

452268.description:

452269.title: Personal Pages

links.title: The Mama On The Rocks
links.description: The Mama on the Rocks is a candid blog by a mother, teacher, and therapist navigating life with a child who has behavioral disorders. She shares unfiltered stories of extreme parenting, mental health struggles, and the daily chaos of family life, offering support and solidarity to others facing similar challenges.

links.title: Perfectly Imperfect Family
links.description: Perfectly Imperfect Family is a heartfelt blog by a mother who is sharing real-life parenting stories, tips for raising ADHD/neurodivergent kids, and practical advice on family life. It celebrates the beauty in everyday chaos and connection.

links.title: The Childhood Collective
links.description: ​The Childhood Collective blog offers science-backed, practical strategies for parents raising children with ADHD. Created by two child psychologists and a speech-language pathologist, the blog provides empathetic guidance to help families navigate ADHD-related challenges at home and school. Resources include parenting tips, executive function support, and tools to foster confidence and connection.

452266.title: Support Groups
452266.description:
Sites in this category serve the support needs of people living with ADD or ADHD.

These groups, communities, or meeting places provide an opportunity for people with a common experience (such as a condition or disease, or a care-giving role) to share their concerns, and to seek and offer information and advice.

Read each site's PRIVACY POLICY carefully, before providing personal information.

These sites are for educational and support purposes only. Please consult your doctor or other health care provider before making any lifestyle changes that may adversely affect your condition.

452247.title: Attachment Disorder
452247.description: Attachment Disorder is a mental illness. It is an emotional problem that occurs in the first three years of life and causes children not to attach and bond to their primary caregiver. Without this fundamental attachment, these children often act out behaviorally and are very difficult to parent.

links.title: Family Attachment Center of Minnesota

links.title: Depression in Children and Teenagers

links.description: Information and activities to help children and adolescents understand clinical and manic depression.

452250.title: Disruptive Behavior Disorders
452250.description:
This category contains information for parents, families, and caregivers, about Disruptive Behavior Disorders.

There are 3 disorders commonly classified in this category:

  • Attention Deficit Disorder
  • Conduct Disorder
  • Oppositional Defiant Disorder

links.title: Conduct Disorder versus Oppositional Defiant Disorder
links.description: Explanation for parents of the similarities and differences of two adolescent behavior disorders.

452252.title: Conduct Disorder
452252.description:
This category contains information for parents, families, and caregivers on Conduct Disorder.

Conduct Disorder is generally considered the most extreme of the Disruptive Behavior Disorders. Behaviors include threatening or harming animals or property; stealing, bullying or lying to get something; and serious violations of rules and laws, such as truancy or running away from home.

links.title: eMedicine:  Conduct Disorder
links.description: Article by W Douglas Tynan, PhD explains one of the most difficult and intractable mental health problems in children and adolescents. Includes definition, progression, comorbidity, school problems, and treatments.

452251.title: Oppositional Defiant Disorder
452251.description:
This category contains information for parents, families, and caregivers on Oppositional Defiant Disorder (ODD).

ODD is defined as when children or teens are extremely oppositional and defiant to authority, usually only at home and school. They still tend to obey the laws of society and don't tend to cause harm to animals, other children, or property.

links.title: Oppositional Defiant Disorder (ODD)

452036.title: Directories

452225.title: Dissociative

452227.title: Dissociative Identity Disorder
452227.description: A controversial topic within mental health, multiple personality refers to what was once called Multiple Personality Disorder, and is now known as Dissociative Identity Disorder.  The diagnosis has detractors, who believe it is iatrogenic (caused by treatment) rather than a "real" disorder.  Just to make the controversy more interesting, many people with multiplicity believe it is not a disorder at all, but a characteristic (like "left-handed"), a way of being that is out of the mainstream.  Post-modern conceptualizations of the self have room for such diversity.        These links cover scholarly, personal, support-group, and philosophical links about multiplicity.

links.title: Sidran Traumatic Stress Foundation
links.description: A non-profit organization and publisher with on-line brochures and articles about DID and other trauma-related disorders, diagnostic materials that are available at cost, and training program. Books can be ordered online.

links.title: Dissociation in the UK

links.title: Astraea's Multiple Personality Resources and Controversies

links.title: Gift Of Many - It Shouldn't Hurt To Be A Child!

links.title: Dissociation.com

links.title: HELP! My Friend Has Multiple Personalities

links.title: Coming Out Multiple

links.title: Basic Information on Dissociative Identity Disorder

links.title: Internet Crisis Center

links.title: Mosaic Minds

452228.title: Web Rings

452201.title: Binge
452201.description: Binge-eating disorder (BED) was identified in 1959 but was not included as a medical diagnostic category until 1994. BED is characterized by frequent episodes of binge eating, occurring at least two days a week for six months.    Binge-eating episodes are associated with at least three of the following:    eating rapidly.   eating until feeling uncomfortably full.   eating when not hungry.   eating alone because of embarrassment.   feeling disgusted, depressed or guilty after overeating.   To meet criteria for BED, a person must also experience marked distress about the binge eating and not regularly engage in self-induced vomiting, fasting or abuse of laxatives or diuretics.    Unlike other eating disorders, such as bulimia nervosa or anorexia nervosa, BED affects a substantial number of men. BED is more common among the severely overweight but can be found among people of any weight. Regardless of a person's weight, it is typical for the BED sufferer to feel overweight and to have a history of many attempts to lose weight. The onset of binge eating is often closely associated with dieting, typically occurring in late adolescence.

452191.description: Pica is an eating disorder (ICD-10: WHO International Classification of Diseases) in which a person repeatedly eats non-food items.   The exact cause of pica is often unknown. It's considered normal for children younger than 18 to 24 months old to put things in their mouths. After this age, eating non-food items is thought to be abnormal. Some people are more likely to have pica: children older than 24 months, pregnant women, especially in rural areas, persons with mental retardation, people with severe psychological problems, people with zinc or iron deficiency.

452237.title: Factitious
452237.description: Factitious disorder is a formal (DSM-IV) mental health diagnosis in which people deliberately exaggerate, fabricate, or induce physical or psychological health problems in themselves in order to get attention for themselves or gain some other form of internal gratification. Munchausen Syndrome is sometimes described as one sub-type of factitious disorder; others say it is another name for this disorder.   Munchausen Syndrome by Proxy (also addressed here)  is a pattern of abusive behavior in which a caretaker deliberately exaggerates, fabricates, or induces physical and/or psychological health problems in <u>another person</u>. This pattern of behavior manifests as physical abuse, sexual abuse, emotional abuse, neglect, or a combination. The primary purpose of this behavior is to gain some form of internal gratification (such as attention) for the perpetrator.

452074.title: Pathological Gambling
452074.description:
Gambling can be defined as playing a game of chance for stakes. Gambling occurs in many forms, most commonly pari-mutuels (horse and dog tracks, off-track-betting parlors, Jai Alai), lotteries, casinos (slot machines, table games), bookmaking (sports books and horse books), card rooms, bingo and the stock market.
Pathological gambling is a progressive disease that devastates not only the gambler but everyone with whom he or she has a significant relationship. In 1980, the American Psychiatric Association accepted pathological gambling as a "disorder of impulse control." It is an illness that is chronic and progressive, but it can be diagnosed and treated.

452066.title: Self Injury
452066.description:
Self Injury can go by many names, such as:
  • Cutting
  • Self Injurious Behavior
  • Deliberate Self Harm
  • Self Inflicted Violence
  • Repetitive Self-Harm Syndrome
Self Injury is far more widespread than is generally realized, especially in adolescents under stress. It also seems to be more common among women, partly because men are more likely to express strong feelings, such as anger, outwardly. However, people from all walks of life self-injure. Many individuals who self-injure believe they are the only person that hurts themselves in this way. Fear, shame and guilt may force people to keep self-injury secret for many years, so when encountering or discovering self-injury it is vital that support and understanding be shown. This means, as well, that the true extent of the disorder is unknown. Research shows that where it is acceptable to talk about, many women, as well as some men, reveal that they have self-injured at some time. Sites included in this category, and its sub-categories, are potentially triggering.

452206.description: Schizotypal personality disorder is a personality disorder that is characterized by a need for social isolation, odd behaviour and thinking, and often unconventional beliefs such as being convinced of having extra sensory abilities. 451966.title: Grief, Loss and Bereavement

Grief is the pain, misery, anguish, suffering, or distress caused by bereavement.

Loss occurs as a result of losing a possession, a person, or can be caused by deprivation or a change of circumstance. Losses can occur through the death of a child, a spouse, a friend, hero, leader, or relative.

Bereavement is caused by loss, especially the loss of a loved one. A loss of position in the community, dignity, security, or reputation can result in feelings of bereavement.

458669.description: Auscultation is the practice of listening, usually with a stethoscope, to the chest.  Two basic sub-categories are 1) heart sounds (and murmurs) and 2) lung sounds.  Auscultation simulators are an attempt to teach medical trainees to recognize what they hear through the stethoscope by providing examples of either actual or simulated sounds.   Simple simulators just provide audio files.  More elaborate simulators allow the user to move the stethoscope over different areas of the chest, provide video or animation of the patient to show venous, arterial, or precordial pulsations, and supplement bedside physical findings with laboratory data such as a phonocardiogram, pressure tracings, echocardiogram, electrocardiogram, and radiology/angiography.

458741.title: Students
458741.description: Student nurses are trainees in preparation for professional nursing practice.   The type of training varies. In other parts of the world, a Bachelor of Nursing degree may be obtained.  Enrolled Nurse (EN) training still exists in many countries.  Some countries train nurses for specific areas of practice, including obstetrics, pediatrics, and mental health.   Postgraduate education in nursing is becoming more common, although nurses undertaking such study are unlikely to be referred to as, "student nurses".
