459116.title: Government Agencies
459116.description: The Occupational Safety and Health Agency (OSHA), a federal entity, is charged with every issue concerning workplace safety, and health. Primarily they are regulatory in nature, but also have enforcement authority. OSHA works with a number of other entities, including subdivisions of the Center for Disease Control.     OSHA, allows states to maintain their own office's of Occupational Safety and Health, through a legislative act. Specifically, Section 18 of the Occupational Safety and Health Act of 1970 (the Act) encourages States to develop and operate their own job safety and health programs.  States must set job safety and health standards that are "at least as effective as" comparable federal standards. (Most States adopt standards identical to federal ones.) States have the option to promulgate standards covering hazards not addressed by federal standards.    Those states that fail to maintain these standards, or those that have significant industrial injuries, again are monitored by OSHA.

458223.title: Cyproterone
458223.description: Cyproterone acetate is an antiandrogen drug used in the treatment of symptoms associated with an excess of androgens, including hirsutism, ovulation problems, and male pattern baldness in women. It is also used in the treatment of prostate cancer.  It may increase the risk of thromboembolic events so the use of oral contraceptives which use this drug in combination with estrogen can bring an increased risk of blood clots.

458224.title: With Ethinyl Estradiol
458224.description: Cyproterone paired with ethinyl estradiol is used in oral contraceptives that also treat the symptoms of hyperandrogenism in women (such as hirsutism and acne).   Cyproterone acts as an antiandrogen (hence it's usefulness in treating acne and other effects of excess androgen) as well as a weak progestin and brings with it an increased risk of blood clots.  Combined with estrogen, with also carries a risk of blood clots, this drug offers an even higher risk of the user developing blood clots.

Designer drugs are illicit variations of other drugs. Because of many different recipes used to manufacture Ecstasy, deaths have been caused by some other substances inadvertently created during production, such as PMA (paramethamphetamine). Ecstasy was banned in 1985, and is currently classified as a Schedule 1 substance.

459014.title: Doula
459014.description:
The Doulas of North America definition:

Doula refers to a supportive companion (other than a friend or loved one) who is professionally trained to provide labor support. She performs no clinical tasks. Doula also refers to lay women who are trained or experienced in providing postpartum care - mother and newborn care, breastfeeding support and advice, cooking, child care, errands, and light cleaning - for the family. To distinguish between the two types of doulas, one may refer to "birth doulas" and " postpartum doulas."

A doula provides:
physical, emotional, and informational support to women and their partners during labor and birth; help and advice on comfort measures such as breathing, relaxation, massage and positioning; assistance to families in gathering information about the course of their labor and their options; continuous emotional reassurance and comfort; non-medical skills such as massage and other non-pharmacological pain relief measures; assistance to partners who want to play an active support role; help so the woman has a safe and satisfying childbirth as the woman defines it.

458961.title: Midwifery
458961.description:
The International Confederation of Midwives definition:

A midwife is a person who, having been regularly admitted to a midwifery education programme, duly recognised in the country in which it is located, has successfully completed the prescribed course of studies in midwifery and has acquired the requisite qualifications to be registered and/or legally licensed to practise midwifery.

She must be able to give the necessary supervision, care and advice to women during pregnancy, labour and the postpartum period, to conduct deliveries on her own responsibility and to care for the newborn and the infant. This care includes preventative measures, the detection of abnormal conditions in mother and child, the procurement of medical assistance and the execution of emergency measures in the absence of medical help. She has an important task in health counselling and education, not only for the women, but also within the family and the community. The work work should involve antenatal education and preparation for parenthood and extends to certain areas of gynaecology, family planning and child care. She may practise in hospitals, clinics, health units, domiciliary conditions or in any other service.

459001.title: Physician Assistant
459001.description: Physician Assistant   (aka: Physician Associate)     The physician assistant role, legally associated with a supervising physician, has allowed PAs to perform tasks previously only performed by doctors: history taking, physical examination, diagnosis, and patient management. Numerous studies have documented the ability of PAs to provide high-quality health care, comparable to that of a physician, for about 80% of the conditions seen in primary care settings. The physician assistant is prepared, both academically and clinically, to provide health care services with the direction and responsible supervision of a Doctor of Medicine (MD) or Osteopathy (DO). PA functions include performing diagnostic, therapeutic, preventive, and health maintenance services.

455079.title: Fire Fighting
455079.description:
The Fireman's Creed " I have no ambition in this world but one, and that is to be a fireman. The position may, in the eyes of some, appear to be a lowly one, but we who know the work which a fireman has to do believe that is a noble calling. There is an adage which says that 'Nothing can be destroyed except by fire'. We strive to preserve from destruction the wealth of the world, which is the product of the industry of men, necessary for the comfort of both the rich and the poor. We are the defenders from fire, of the art which has beautified the world, the product of the genius of men and the means of refinement of mankind. But, above all, our proudest endeavor is to save lives of men ~ the work of God Himself. Under the impulse of such thoughts, the nobility of the occupation thrills us and stimulates us to deeds of daring, even at the supreme sacrifice. Such considerations may not strike the average mind, but they are sufficient to fill to the limit our ambition in life and to make us serve the general purpose of human society." - Edward F. Croker, Chief of Department F.D.N.Y. - 1898

454790.title: Reproductive Health
454790.description: Reproductive health is defined by the World Health Organization as a state of physical, mental, and social well-being in all matters relating to the reproductive system at all stages of life. Reproductive health implies that people are able to have a satisfying and safe sex life and that they have the capability to reproduce and the freedom to decide if, when, and how often to do so. Implicit in this are the right of men and women to be informed and to have access to safe, effective, affordable, and acceptable methods of family planning of their choice, and the right to appropriate health-care services that enable women to safely go through pregnancy and childbirth.

455030.title: Hypnosis and Imagery
455030.description: Hypnosis and imagery are tools and methods used to prepare for childbirth.  It is generally felt that stress, fear and tension contribute significantly to the pain during childbirth.  The mother learns how to go into hypnosis so that she can more effectively cope with labor.  This allows her to be responsive during labor, with less pain.  Hypnosis and imagery advocates claim benefits such as shorter labors, less need for intervention, reduced risk of perineal tears, episiotomy and C-section, largely due to the mother's deep relaxation and during labor and birth. These methods are similar to birth education programs (such as Lamaze or Bradley) and provide the woman with more specific techniques of controlling pain, doubt and fear while she labors, pushes, and communicates with her baby, birth partner, midwife or physician.

455019.title: Obstetric Fistula
455019.description:
Obstetric fistula is a condition almost unknown in the West but indescribably hideous for millions of sufferers in the poorest countries in the world.

It typically occurs when a teenage girl cannot deliver a baby because it is too big for her pelvis. After several days of labor without access to a doctor, the baby dies and the girl is left with a hole between her bladder, vagina and sometimes rectum. The result is that urine and sometimes feces drip constantly down her legs. In some cases, she is also left lame from nerve damage.

Women with fistulas stink and leave a trail of urine behind them. They are often abandoned by their husbands and driven out by other villagers.

links.description: Provides education of doctors of optometry who provide quality clinical care and who emphasize a caring and ethical commitment to the welfare of their patients.

links.title: University of Waterloo, School of Optometry
links.description: Ontario, Canada

458850.title: Organizations
458850.description: This category is for associations and organizations that represent vision care professionals, makers of corrective lenses, or people who are visually impaired. If this does not describe your site, please submit it to the appropriate category.

links.title: International Council for Education of People with Visual Impairment, European Region
links.description: Shares information and knowledge on the field of education and rehabilitation of people with visual impairment.

links.title: Lighthouse Guild
links.description: Worldwide organization dedicated to overcoming vision impairment through rehabilitation, education, research and advocacy.

links.title: International Association of Contact Lens Educators (IACLE)
links.description: Global educational organisation dedicated to raising the standard of contact lens education worldwide and promoting the widespread, safe use of contact lenses.

links.title: British Contact Lens Association
links.description: Information about the association. Clinical Conference announcements, continuing education courses and scientific meetings.

links.title: International Society for Clinical Electrophysiology of Vision
links.description: ISCEV promotes knowledge and cooperation in field of clinical and basic electrophysiology of vision.

links.title: International Society for Eye Research
links.description: Dealing with ocular research and news updates.

links.title: International Uveitis Study Group (IUSG)
links.description: Researchers and clinicians engaged in research and clinical management of uveitis.

links.title: Sight and Hearing Association
links.description: Dedicated to preventing the needless loss of vision and hearing through effective screening, education, and research. This site provides public information about eye and ear topics as well as information regarding products and services.

links.title: Sjogren's Syndrome Foundation
links.description: Offers education and support, and strives to increase awareness and research into more effective treatments and a cure.

links.title: Talking Newspaper Association UK
links.description: Provides national and regional talking newspapers and magazines in alternative formats for the blind, visually impaired and the disabled who find it difficult to hold a newspaper.

links.title: Tear Film & Ocular Surface Society
links.description: The official website of the Tear Film and Ocular Surface Society.

links.title: Vitreo Retina Society of India
links.description: Promotes the practice and research of the diseases of retina and vitreous.

links.title: American Uveitis Society
links.description: A resource for researchers in inflammatory eye diseases.

links.title: National Alliance for Eye and Vision Research
links.description: Non-profit advocacy organization made up of a coalition of professional, consumer, and industry organizations involved in research in eye and vision disorders.

links.title: Lions World Vision Institute
links.description: Non-profit charitable organization dedicated to the recovery, evaluation and distribution of eye tissue for transplantation, research and education.

links.title: Council for Refractive Surgery Quality Assurance
links.description: Consumer organization providing information about wavefront, LASIK, and other refractive surgery techniques. Includes a database of certified practitioners.

links.title: Cochrane Eyes and Vision Group  (CEVG)
links.description: International network of individuals working to prepare, maintain and promote access to systematic reviews of interventions to treat or prevent eye diseases or visual impairment.

links.title: Fight for Sight
links.description: A non-profit organization funding fellowships and grants for vision research and children's eye clinics in the U.S. and internationally to prevent blindness and find cures for all eye diseases.

links.title: Vision Australia Foundation
links.description: Not for profit organisation providing services, facilities, and information to visually impaired persons. Contact and location details, resource list, professional and business service information, and library of Braille, audio, or large print format details included.

links.title: The Vision Council
links.description: Optical trade organization dedicated to educating the public about eye health and eyewear. Tips on choosing the most attractive eyeglasses for the shape of your face.

links.title: Collaborative Ocular Melanoma Study
links.description: A multicenter randomized  trial sponsored by The National Eye Institute and The National Cancer Institute of the National Institutes of Health.

links.title: Stanford Vision and Imaging Science and Technology
links.description: Research activities span topics in the areas of human visual sensing and electronic imaging.

links.title: Lions Vision Research Foundation, Inc.
links.description: Supports low vision research and rehabilitation to minimize the disabilities caused by low vision and blindness. Objectives met through partnership with low vision clinic at the Wilmer Eye Institute.

452368.title: Services
452368.description: This category includes sites relevant to services associated with a variety of health issues. Future subcategories will organize any additional miscellaneous health service topics not generally appearing in other health or medical categories.       Not for hospitals, medical clinics, medical doctors' offices, medical laboratories, weight loss centers, physical fitness centers.

452370.title: Health Records Services
452370.description: For businesses offering Medical Records services to the public.

links.title: MedXchange
links.description: Information about the services offered which include a health portfolio, medical data and security and safety. Gives benefits, costs and terms and conditions.

links.title: Medical I. D Card
links.description: A wallet size card with your medical information that can mean the difference between life and death during an emergency situation.

links.title: Healthgram
links.description: Portable health record to store personal health information and test results in a safe and secure way.

links.title: People Chart
links.description: Provides a service that helps patients gather and use their medical records to improve their health care at home and while traveling.

links.title: Health Records for Families
links.description: Guide to keeping your own health records online.

links.title: EDocAmerica.com
links.description: Subscription-based medical advice for companies and their employees.

links.title: The Analyst - Online Health Evaluations
links.description: Online analysis of symptoms, lifestyle, risk factors and personal and family medical history. Fee based.

links.title: Best Doctors
links.description: Comprehensive fee-based medical referral service.

links.title: Ask The Doctor
links.description: Previous answers and easy access to personal advice and information at your request from Dr. Suneel Sharman.

links.title: PinkWhale Healthcare
links.description: An e-health company offering online and telephone based personal healthcare services. Ask physician or a specialist a question. Contains profiles with credentials details.  Karnataka, India.

links.title: Body Calculator
links.description: Shows your BMR, BMI, menstrual, WHR, body fat, and biorhythm calculators.

454235.title: Specific Substances
454235.description:
The Specific Substances category focuses on health issues related to substances humans deliberately put into their bodies. Sites appropriate for this category include consumer information, professional information, organizations, services, and personal experiences. Sites not listed in this category:

  • Topics related to public policy issues are organized in Society: Issues: Health.
  • Topics related to environmental exposure to toxic substances are organized in Science: Environment: Environmental Health: Toxic Substances.
  • Topics related to occupational exposure to hazardous substances are organized in Health: Occupational Health and Safety: Hazardous Substances.
  • Topics related to drugs and medications synthesized and manufactured for treating specific conditions and diseases are organized in Health: Pharmacy: Drugs and Medications.
  • Topics related to herbal medications are organized in Health: Alternative: Herbs.
  • Online retailers of products are organized in Shopping.

454272.title: Alcoholic Beverages
454272.description:
The Alcoholic Beverages category focuses on the effects of alcoholic beverages on the human body. Sites appropriate for this category include consumer information, professional information, organizations, services, and personal experiences.

Sites not listed in this category:
  • Topics focused on public policy issues are listed in Society: Issues: Health: Alcohol.

links.title: AIM
links.description: Alcohol In Moderation is an organization promoting a sensible and moderate drinking message. Information from scientific researchers, the beverage alcohol industry and associations, on research, health issues and legislation.

links.title: Eurekalert: Light-to-Moderate Drinking Appears to Have Little Effect on the Risk for Breast Cancer
links.description: A new study in 'Alcoholism: Clinical and Experimental Research' confirms that heavy drinking increases risk for breast cancer, but that light to moderate drinking appears to have little effect on a woman's risk for breast cancer.

links.title: BBC News - A daily drink 'only good for men'
links.description: Covers research showing that drinking alcohol daily protects against heart disease in men but not in women.

links.title: Drink Aware
links.description: Raising awareness about alcohol, health issues, legislation and drinking. Find useful information on binge drinking, hangover remedies and the health effects of alcohol.

454273.title: Benefits
454273.description: Lists websites and articles focusing on the positive effects of alcoholic beverages on health.

links.title: JAMA: Moderate Alcohol Consumption and Risk of Heart Failure Among Older Persons
links.description: Increasing levels of moderate alcohol consumption are associated with a decreasing risk of heart failure among older persons. Journal of the American Medical Association.

links.title: JAMA: Protective Effects of Moderate Alcohol Consumption on Ischemic Stroke
links.description: The protective effect of moderate consumption of alcohol was found in various populations. Journal of the American Medical Association.

links.title: Medical News Today: Moderate Drinking Raises Hormone that Protects from Artery Disease
links.description: A study done at TNO Nutrition and Food Research, Netherlands suggests that moderate drinkers have better hormone levels than heavy drinkers or people who do not drink any alcohol at all.

links.title: CNN.com: Light Drinking May Cut Stroke Risk
links.description: Studies have indicated that drinking alcohol in moderation can cut heart attack risks, and new research supports the theory that the same holds true for preventing strokes.

links.title: ScienceDaily: Alcohol Linked to Decreased Hypertension Risk in Young Women
links.description: Researchers at the Massachusetts General Hospital and Brigham and Women's Hospital in the US find that moderate alcohol consumption in women was beneficial to blood pressure and at high levels it was harmful.

454275.title: Beer
454275.description: Lists websites and articles focusing on the positive effects of beer on health.

links.title: AskMen.com: The Benefits of Beer
links.description: Medical benefits of drinking beer.

links.title: BBC News: Guinness good for you - official
links.description: Research indicates a pint of stout may be as effective as a daily aspirin in preventing coronary blood clots.

links.title: The University of Western Ontario -  Study Shows Beer Has Same Benefits As Red Wine
links.description: Press release describing the results of the study, which show a glass of beer or stout has the same antioxidant properties as a glass of red wine.

454274.title: Wine
454274.description: Lists websites and articles focusing on the positive effects of wine on health.

links.title: CNN: Wine Industry Trumpets Anti-Bacteria Research
links.description: West Virginia University researcher suggests that one to two glasses of wine with meals may help wipe out bacterial food contamination.

links.title: CNN: Study Links Moderate Wine Drinking, Lower Stroke Risk
links.description: A 16-year study of 13,000 people in Denmark finds that a weekly intake of wine significantly reduces the risk of stroke.

links.title: BBC News: Wine Prevents Repeat Heart Attack
links.description: Reports a study published in the journal Circulation that suggests sensible wine consumption among middle-aged men who have had a heart attack will reduce the risk of a second one.

links.title: BBC News: Why Red Wine is Healthier
links.description: Article reporting on a study which explains some of the reasons why red wine appears to protect the heart.

links.title: BBC News: Red Wine 'Protects From Colds'
links.description: Report on a study that moderate consumption of wine, especially red wine, helps fight off the common cold.

links.title: BBC News: Red Wine 'Can Stop Herpes'
links.description: US-based study finds that red wine could prevent the spread of herpes.

links.title: BBC News: A Daily Dose of Wine Could Improve the Brain
links.description: Reports on an Italian study which finds that resveratrol, found in wine, helps to regenerate neural cells.

links.title: ScienceDaily: Wine Drinkers Have Healthier Lifestyles
links.description: Study reported in the American Journal Of Clinical Nutrition suggests that the benefits of wine drinking may not be only physiological, but that a preference for wine may be part of an overall healthier lifestyle.

links.title: ScienceDaily: Drinking Wine, Particularly White Wine, May Help Keep Lungs Healthy
links.description: A University at Buffalo study has shown that drinking wine -- especially white -- recently and over a lifetime, was associated with better lung function.

links.title: ScienceDaily: Wine Drinking May Reduce Colon Cancer Risk
links.description: Study at the State University of New York showed that drinking at least one glass of wine per week may protect against the development of colo-rectal cancer, whereas beer or mixed drinks do not.

links.title: ScienceDaily: Red Wine's Health Benefits May be Due in Part to "Estrogen" in Grape Skin
links.description: Northwestern University Medical School researchers have found that resveratrol, a form of estrogen found in red grapes and wine, may be responsible for wine's anti-carcinogenic and anti-arteriosclerotic properties.

links.title: ScienceDaily: Drinking Wine May Lower Risk Of Dementia
links.description: A study by the Institute of Preventive Medicine in Denmark, reported in the scientific journal Neurology, shows that flavonoids in wine may protect against Alzheimer's disease and stroke-caused mental deterioration.

links.title: ScienceDaily: New Cholesterol Fighter Found in Red Wine
links.description: Scientists at the University of California, Davis, have identified another group of chemicals in red wine, saponins, that are linked to the ability to lower cholesterol. The study was reported at a meeting of the American Chemical Society.

links.title: MedicineNet.com: Cancer Prevention and Red Wine
links.description: Summarizes the current state of knowledge mainly about the effect of red wine polyphenols on cancer in humans.

links.title: UC Davis: Tumors in Mice Delayed by Red Wine Component, Study Shows
links.description: Catechin, a potent antioxidant found in red wine, delayed tumor formation when fed to mice that are predisposed to developing tumors, report researchers at the University of California, Davis.

links.title: Wine and Health Summit
links.description: Biennial US-based event for physicians and connoisseurs, highlighting current research on wine and cardiovascular health.

links.title: WebMD: Bottoms Up
links.description: Article summarizes some of the beneficial effects of moderate wine consumption on cardiovascular disease, cancer, and osteoporosis.

links.title: The Guardian: Two Glasses of Wine a Week Still Safe for Pregnant Women
links.description: The UK Department of Health rejects claims that the only safe choice for pregnant women and those hoping to conceive is abstention from beverage alcohol. Article also explains the opposing view.

links.title: Phystech Portal: Food Scientist Developing Wine-Based Disinfectant
links.description: Scientists at Oregon State University explore wine's antiseptic effects on E. coli and salmonella, and speculate on developing a wine-based anti-microbial spray.

links.title: eMedicine.com: Alcohol Intoxication
links.description: Includes definition, signs and symptoms, treatment, physician diagnosis, information about drunk driving, photos of liver damage, and bibliography. Article by James S Cohen, MD.

links.title: Drinking Without Food may set you up for High Blood Pressure
links.description: An epidemiological study conducted by the University at Buffalo suggests that moderate to high consumption of all kinds of alcoholic beverages without accompanying food consumption is a significant risk factor in developing hypertension.

links.title: MedlinePlus Medical Encyclopedia: Alcohol Withdrawal
links.description: Overview, including definition, causes, incidence, risk factors, symptoms, signs, and treatment. Provided by the U.S. National Library of Medicine.

links.title: Alcohol Withdrawal Syndrome
links.description: Information about the syndrome, and what doctors, family, and friends can do to help. Provided by the American Academy of Family Physicians.

links.title: Cannabis
links.description: Information on marijuana, how it is taken, and effects it has on the body.

links.title: Marijuana and the Developing Brain
links.description: More states are legalizing marijuana, but concerns remain about its long-term effects on the adolescent brain. From American Psychological Association magazine.

links.title: Chocolate 'Fights' Tooth Decay
links.description: A study by researchers at Osaka University in Japan found that parts of the cocoa bean thwart mouth bacteria and tooth decay. Reported by BBC News.

links.title: The Sweet Lure of Chocolate
links.description: Information about cacao, history, production, and health effects. Includes bibliography and links to related material. Provided by the Exporatorium, a science museum in San Francisco.

links.title: Discovering the Sweet Mysteries of Chocolate
links.description: Summary of available information about history, cravings, and effects on the nervous system. Links to references.

links.title: Chocolate Does A Man's Heart Good
links.description: Report at Forbes.com on a study showing that chocolate may improve the cardiovascular health of men.

links.title: International Journal of Medical Sciences: Flavanols in cocoa
links.description: Report on studies providing clinical evidences that flavanol may enhance brain blood flow, improve cognitive health and offer other benefits.

links.title: Ill Effects of Caffeine and How to Quit Coffee
links.description: Information about symptoms of caffeine addiction, calculating daily intake, withdrawal symptoms, and quitting gradually.

links.title: JAMA: Coffee Consumption and Risk of Type 2 Diabetes
links.description: A study published in the Journal of the American Medical Association reports an association between coffee consumption and a reduced risk of diabetes in a Finnish population.

links.title: JAMA: Association of Coffee and Caffeine Intake With the Risk of Parkinson Disease
links.description: Higher coffee and caffeine intake is associated with a lower incidence of Parkinson Disease in a study of Japanese-American men. Published in the Journal of the American Medical Association.

links.title: JAMA: Coffee Consumption and Symptomatic Gallstone Disease in Men
links.description: In a study of men in the United States, coffee consumption may have helped to prevent symptomatic gallstone disease. Published in the Journal of the American Medical Association,

links.title: The Coffee Review - Reference
links.description: Browse hundreds of pages of informative coffee materials adapted from Kenneth Davids' books.   Includes a section on coffee and health.

links.title: New Scientist: Coffee Drinkers Have Lower Diabetes Risk
links.description: In a Dutch population, drinkers of seven or more cups of coffee a day were half as likely to develop type 2 diabetes. Journal reference: Lancet (vol 360, p 1477).

links.title: Institute for Scientific Information on Coffee
links.description: Answers to questions about the effects of coffee on health, provided by the Institute for Scientific Information on Coffee.

links.title: Cranberry May Offer Protection Against Antibiotic-Resistant Bacteria
links.description: Study of cranberry juice and bacteria, with public health implications. Beneficial effect against urinary tract infections may start within two hours. June 19, 2002.

links.title: Herbs at a Glance: Cranberry
links.description: Information about research, uses, side effects, and cautions, from the National Center for Complementary and Alternative Medicine.

454238.title: Dairy Products
454238.description:
The Dairy Products category focuses on health issues related to the consumption of dairy products, such as milk, cheese, and yogurt. Sites appropriate for this category include consumer information, professional information, organizations, services, and personal experiences. Sites not listed in this category:

  • Topics related to cooking with dairy products are organized in Home: Cooking: Dairy.
  • Topics related to cooking without dairy products are organized in Home: Cooking: Special Diets: Dairy-Free.
  • Manufacturers of dairy products are included in Business: Food and Related Products: Dairy.
  • Businesses related to dairy livestock production are included in Business: Agriculture and Forestry: Livestock: Dairy.
  • Sites which focus on the welfare of dairy animals are included in Society: Issues: Animal Welfare: Farming.
  • Online retailers of dairy products are included in Shopping: Food.
  • Sites which focus on allergies to dairy products are included in Health: Conditions and Diseases: Allergies: Food: Milk.
  • Sites which focus on lactose intolerance are included in Health: Conditions and Diseases: Digestive Disorders: Intestinal: Lactose Intolerance.

links.title: MedlinePlus: Cow's Milk for Infants and Children
links.description: Recommendation from the American Academy of Pediatricians that infants not be given milk. Includes suggested daily consumption of dairy products for infants, children, and adults.

links.title: Milk: Polyunsaturated Non Adventures In Paradise
links.description: Brief history of milk production and consumption, including  health issues.

454239.title: Effects
454239.description: The effects of dairy product consumption on health.

links.title: AJCN: Dairy Foods and Bone Health: Examination of the Evidence
links.description: Review by Roland L. Weinsier and Carlos L. Krumdieck to determine whether scientific evidence supports the recommendation that dairy foods be consumed daily for improved bone health in the general US population.

links.title: Effect of Dietary Calcium and Milk Consumption on Risk of Thromboembolic Stroke in Older Middle-aged Men
links.description: Examination of the effect of baseline dietary calcium and milk intake on stroke risk in 22 years of follow-up in 3150 men 55 to 68 years old.

454240.title: Benefits
454240.description: The health benefits of dairy product consumption.

links.title: PubMed: The Norwegian Women and Cancer Study
links.description: Cohort study of 48,844 premenopausal Norwegian women that  examined the relationship between childhood and adult milk consumption and breast cancer incidence.

454241.title: Detriments
454241.description: The health detriments of dairy product consumption.

links.title: The Milk Letter - A Message to My Patients
links.description: A letter from a breast cancer surgeon to his patients.

links.title: Milk: The Perfect Food - For Cows
links.description: Christina Pirello explains the basic health and nutritional reasons humans should avoid consumption of dairy products.

links.title: PCRM - Health Concerns About Dairy
links.description: Bone health, calcium intake and osteoporosis, and dairy consumption's relationship to diabetes, cancer, cardiovascular disease, and other disorders. Includes news releases, fact sheets, and dairy-free recipes.

links.title: PubMed:   A Geographic Approach to Senile Cataracts
links.description: F.J. Simmoons examination of evidence for the hypothesis that some types of senile cataracts may be brought on by decades-long consumption of milk and milk products.

links.title: Not Milk
links.description: Provides list of famous people and organizations who support and oppose milk consumption, offers short articles claiming health problems from milk, and provides links.

links.title: The Free Library - Cows' Milk, Diabetes Connection Bolstered
links.description: Report on Finnish research which studied babies from diabetes-prone families and their immune system reactions to the milk protein bovine insulin.

454242.title: IGF-1
454242.description: Insulin-like Growth Factor-1 (IGF-1) is a hormone that appears naturally in humans and cows.  It is present in high levels in milk from cows treated with recombinant Bovine Growth Hormone (rBGH).

links.title: Europa: Growth Promoting Hormones Pose Health Risk to Consumers
links.description: The EU Scientific Committee on Veterinary Measures relating to Public Health confirmed that the use of hormones as growth promoters for cattle poses a potential health risk to consumers.

links.title: NCI Fact Sheet: Tea and Cancer Prevention
links.description: Summary information from the National Cancer Institute describes antioxidents, laboratory findings, human studies, and research.

links.title: Wikipedia: Health Effects of Tea
links.description: Often-changing article about both positive and negative health effects of tea, with extensive citations.

links.title: Types of Tea and Their Health Benefits
links.description: Overview of the health benefits of different varieties of tea, with an emphasis on findings backed by scientific evidence.

links.title: Tea - Micronutrient Information Center - Linus Pauling Institute at Oregon State University
links.description: A detailed overview of the body of scientific knowledge pertaining to tea and health, with 84 references to studies and scientific articles.

454267.title: Conferences
454267.description: Research or Health Conferences on Tobacco, Smoking, Tobacco Policy, Tobacco Control, Cessation, and so on.

454246.title: Effects
454246.description:
The Effects category focuses on tobacco-related effects on the human body. Sites appropriate for this category include consumer information, professional information, organizations, services, and personal experiences.

The primary method of organizing this information is by the type of tobacco-related effect. The types of effects include, but are not limited to:

  • Cancer,
  • Effects on the respiratory system,
  • Effects on the cardiovascular system,
  • Effects on the brain and nervous system,
  • Effects on the mouth and throat, and
  • Effects on reproduction and pregnancy.
Some sites focus on all effects resulting from a specific type of exposure. These are organized under "By Source of Exposure" and include:
  • Cigarette smoking,
  • Cigar and pipe smoking,
  • Smokeless tobacco, and
  • Secondhand smoke.
Sites not listed in this category:
  • Topics focused on addiction are listed in Health: Addictions: Substance Abuse: Tobacco.
  • Topics focused on public policy issues are listed in Society: Issues: Health: Tobacco.

links.title: Very Well - Smoking-Related Diseases
links.description: Links and resources about the effects of secondhand smoke, passive smoking and smoking related diseases.

links.title: Tobacco Facts
links.description: The facts on tobacco products and cancer of the larynx, lung, and mouth, emphysema, epidemology, and how to quit; information and graphic pictures from a Kentucky physician.

links.title: Cigarette Anyone?
links.description: Firsthand accounts of what it is like to live with the diseases caused by cigarettes.

links.title: BBC News: Grim toll of smoking
links.description: More than 122,000 British smokers will die prematurely in the year 2000 from a smoking-related disease; article explains.

links.title: Smoking Increases Anxiety
links.description: Smoking is supposed to calm the nerves, but researchers have found evidence that it might have the opposite effect. BBS News article on recent research.

links.title: Worldwide Trends in Tobacco Consumption and Mortality
links.description: WHO report outlines effects of tobacco globally, identifies trends.

links.title: The Whole Truth About Smoking
links.description: New research find that the tobacco industry does a good job in deceiving the public about the full health risks of smoking; a rundown of 6 myths about smoking and the facts.

links.title: Mortality from Smoking in Developed Countries 1950-2000
links.description: Latest edition of massive tome; content in PDF format.

links.title: Cigarette Smoking-Attributable Morbidity --- United States, 2000
links.description: Most reports focus on how many people are killed by tobacco products; this report estimates how much disease cigarettes cause: tobacco products give more than 8.6 million Americans serious diseases every year.

links.title: Smoking Deaths Not Overstated, Re-Analysis Shows
links.description: Refuting claims by the tobacco industry that death estimates from smoking are inflated, the American Medical Association re-analyzes the data.

links.title: Diagnose-Me: Conditions: Cigarette Smoke Damage
links.description: Lists diseases caused by tobacco propducts, and provides a brief description of each.

links.title: Smoking Cessation Health Center
links.description: Discussion, graphics, and analysis of tobacco use, disease, and death.

links.title: Smoking Caused Disability
links.description: Smoking not only shortens life, it increases number of years of disability.  This research analysis estimates how much increased disability is caused by smoking.

links.title: Cognitive Effects of Nicotine
links.description: Report on studies of nicotine and other nicotinic agonists on improving performance on attention and memory tasks, as well as on treating Alzheimer's disease, schizophrenia, and attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder.

links.title: Nicotine Metabolite Shows Promise for Improving Memory, Protecting Brain Cells
links.description: Report that a nicotine metabolite may improve memory and protect brain cells from diseases such as Alzheimer's and Parkinson's. The researcher is Dr. Jerry J. Buccafusco, director of the Alzheimer's Research Center at the Medical College of Georgia.

links.title: Nicotine-Like Drugs Can Enhance Learning and Memory
links.description: Report by Duke University behavioral pharmacologist Edward Levin that nicotine-like compounds help restore the ability to learn and remember in rats that have brain lesions similar to those found in Alzheimer's disease patients. Reported in Science Daily News.

links.title: BBC News: Nicotine Help for Tourette's
links.description: Nicotine patches may help patients with Tourette's syndrome control involuntary movements.

links.title: Smoking Causes Mental Decline
links.description: Recent research finds cigarettes cause faster mental decline as smokers get older.

454247.title: By Source of Exposure
454247.description:
The By Source of Exposure category focuses on health effects due to specific sources of exposure to tobacco products, including:

  • Cigarette smoking,
  • Cigar smoking,
  • Pipe smoking,
  • Smokeless tobacco, and
  • Secondhand smoke.
Sites not listed in this category:
  • Topics focused on specific types of tobacco-related effects are organized in Health: Specific Substances: Tobacco: Effects.
  • Topics focused on public policy issues are listed in Society: Issues: Health: Tobacco.

454253.title: Cigar and Pipe Smoking
454253.description: Sites about the health effects of smoking cigars and pipes.

links.title: Health Risks Associated With Cigar Smoking
links.description: AMA report summarizes findings from a scientific conference, including cigars cause nicotine addiction and lung cancer.

links.title: Effect of Cigar Smoking on the Risk of Cardiovascular Disease, Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease and Cancer in Men
links.description: Summary of June 1999 article in the New England Journal of Medicine covers what cigars do to the heart, lungs, and throat.

links.title: Pipe Smoking and Health
links.description: An MD examines the risks and benefits of pipe smoking in terms of health and well being.

links.title: Cigars and Tobacco-related Cancers
links.description: Scientific paper estimates the effects of cigars; covers the death caused, not disease.

454254.title: Cigarette Smoking
454254.description: Sites about the health effects of smoking cigarettes.

links.title: The Safer Cigarette: What the Tobacco Industry Could Do..and Why It Hasn't Done it
links.description: ASH-UK paper; a survey of 25 years of patents for innovations to reduce toxic and carcinogenic chemicals in tobacco smoke.

links.title: Why Low Tar Cigarettes Don't Work and How the Tobacco Industry Has Fooled the Smoking Public
links.description: Smokers could be forgiven for believing that low tar cigarettes deliver less tar to the smoker's lung. However, the actual tar exposure, and hence health risk, from smoking low tar brands may be the almost the same as for conventional cigarettes.  ASH-UK report.

links.title: Cigarettes With Defective Filters Sold For 40 Years
links.description: Philip Morris knowingly marketed cigarettes with defective filters for 40 years, according to recent research.

links.title: Cigarettes Engineered for Addiction
links.description: BBC News article on substances added to cigarettes by the industry to increase their addictiveness.

links.title: ScienceDaily Magazine -- Tobacco Smoke Flavoring Contains Hazardous Chemicals
links.description: Scientists have new data that toxic flavoring chemicals put in cigarettes are reaching smokers through cigarette smoke and may pose health hazards of their own.

links.title: Cigarettes: a Complex Cocktail of Chemicals
links.description: BBC Report. More than 600 substances can be legally added to cigarettes, many of which act to increase the addictive impact of nicotine.

links.title: Researcher Publishes First Measurements of 'Free-base' Nicotine in Cigarette Smoke
links.description: Research measures a more highly addictive form of nicotine in cigarettes and finds that "the modern cigarette does to nicotine what crack does to cocaine".

links.title: Cigarettes are Nicotine Delivery Devices
links.description: Collection of FDA papers in PDF format, much of which concerns design and manufacture of cigarettes.

links.title: A Safer Cigarette? Prove It, Say Critics
links.description: JAMA article provides scientific evaluation of claims R.J. Reynold is making about its new tobacco product.

links.title: FTC Accepts Settlements of Charges that "Alternative" Cigarette Ads Are Deceptive
links.description: FTC action highlights claims made by makers of "natural" or "no additives" cigarettes.

links.title: Prying Open the Door to the Tobacco Industry's Secrets About Nicotine
links.description: Article in medical journal surveys industry documents produced in litigation, and finds the tobacco industry knew for decades that nicotine is an addictive drug, and knew ways to design cigarettes to make them more addictive.

links.title: Smoking Kills: The Tobacco White Paper

1031703.title: Hookah
1031703.description:
A hookah (waterpipe, narghile, arghila, kalian, qalyan or shisha) is a single- or multi-stemmed instrument for vaporizing and smoking flavored tobacco called shisha in which the vapor or smoke is passed through a water basin (often glass-based) before inhalation.

When a waterpipe is used to produce smoke (as is common in the Arab States of the Persian Gulf), it is usually referred to as a hookah, which means "jar" in Arabic. When the same device is used to vaporize shisha (as is common in India and the Levant), it is usually referred to as a nargile, which means "gourd" in Sanskrit.
The vapor from a nargile looks similar enough to the smoke from a hookah as to cause both users and medical professionals to often confuse the two.

This category is for sites about the recreational use of hookah and other types of water pipes.

452310.title: Chronic Pain
452310.description: Sites in this category aim to serve the support needs of people suffering with the debilitating effects of Chronic Pain, and those who are searching for effective methods of pain management.      Chronic pain is a condition which persists for one to three months beyond the time that an expected acute pain or acute injury should subside or is associated with a chronic pathological process.   Pain management can be defined as the combination of various psychological techniques and practical strategies designed to optimize physical function, quality of life and to reduce emotional distress for people suffering with the effects of chronic pain.    The materials contained within these sites are not intended to replace professional medical care or attention by a qualified practitioner. 454318.title: Pelvic Inflammatory Disease
454318.description: Pelvic inflammatory disease (often abbreviated as PID) is a result of untreated infections, most commonly chlamydia and gonorrhea.  It most commonly appears as an infection of the fallopian tubes (salpingitis) or the lining of the uterus (endometritis) and can cause extensive pelvic scarring.  It can lead to such complications as infertility, higher risk of ectopic (tubal) pregnancy and chronic pelvic pain.

454303.title: Endometriosis
454303.description: Endometriosis is a condition in which tissues like those which line the uterus are found outside the uterus.These misplaced tissues develop into growths or lesions which respond to the menstrual cycle: each month the tissues build up, break down, and shed. Menstrual blood flows from the uterus and out of the body through the vagina, but the blood and tissue shed from endometrial growths have no way of leaving the body. This results in internal bleeding which can cause pain, infertility, scar tissue formation, adhesions, and bowel problems.
